candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis requires three components: acute epididymal orchitis, testicular infarction, and P. aeruginosa as the causative agent. C001 correctly identifies bacterial epididymo-orchitis but does not specify the organism nor include the testicular infarction that is confirmed by MRI non-enhancement and pathological hemorrhagic infarction findings in this case.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Captures epididymo-orchitis (bacterial) but omits the specific causative organism (Pseudomonas aeruginosa) and the critical complication of testicular infarction

case_quality_flags: Unusual etiology: P. aeruginosa epididymo-orchitis with testicular infarction in a 13-year-old is rare; concurrent occult penis noted as incidental finding
Testicular infarction confirmed by MRI at 60 days and pathology, making it a required component of the final diagnosis
